reason: The claims check out. (1) The insertion gate is per dataset and uses kernel elapsed >= 28800 s (build_probe_kernel.py l.1423-1434), so upstream slack before the gate is 8.0 minus 7.36-7.74 h, which is 0.26-0.64 h. The ~4 h headroom exists only after the CSV is written. coordinject runs there, with a 37800 s deadline, a per-worker rule that starts no new video once 1.25 x its slowest video would pass the deadline, a kill at deadline + 900 s, and fail-soft behaviour (coordinject_patch.py l.1-27, l.257-273). (2) Dummy wall time does not predict the scoring latency. The ledger and CONTEXT numbers match the finding, and the rank order even inverts: exp70a had a 1,629 s dummy but the fastest latency, (6.87, 7.04] h, while exp70d had a 1,320 s dummy and a latency of (7.19, 7.36] h. (3) A speed lever such as fp16 or fewer TTA views would change the node set. That makes it a new mechanism after the R8 line, so it stays closed. Three corrections, none of which change the verdict. (a) The '+1.7 h' coordinject cost is too low. The hidden set has 100-130 videos, up to 65 per worker, and at 130 s each that is ~2.35 h. 7.74 + 2.35 = 10.09 h, which is still under the 10.5 h guard. At the 7.74 h baseline, full coverage needs <= ~153 s per video, not the ~165 s derived at 7.5 h. Going over that gives partial coverage, not a timeout. (b) tools/runtime_ledger.py l.252-257 already labels L > 8.0 h as 'insertion gate MAY have fired'. The new part is the rule for interpreting that label. (c) Ledger latency counts from submission to completion, so it includes queue and scoring time. That makes the > 8.0 h upper-bound trigger conservative: it can flag a run the gate did not affect, but it cannot miss one the gate did.
fix: Adopt the finding, with these changes. (1) Before probe 46 scores (expected ~22:00-22:30Z), pre-register in CONTEXT: if the exp70q ledger upper bound is > 8.0 h, which the ledger prints as 'MAY have fired', label its score 'possibly confounded by the insertion gate' and do not use it to open or close the cap/threshold line. Upgrade the label to 'confounded' only if the kernel log shows 'DIVINS SKIPPED (deadline)'; if the log can be pulled, check it. (2) exp75 runtime gate: mean per-video COORDINJECT_WORKER seconds on the dummy <= 130 s is PASS, 130-150 s is acceptable with partial-coverage risk, and > 150 s means partial coverage is likely. Any stack with a division rung must recompute the bound as (10.5 h - that rung's measured L upper bound) / 65 videos. Never gate on dummy wall time. (3) Template text: 'headroom only post-CSV (coordinject-type stages, fail-soft guard at 10.5 h); upstream slack ~0.26-0.64 h before the 8.0 h per-dataset insertion gate'. (4) No speed-lever build.
realistic_gain: 0 LB directly. This is a procedure and interpretation guard. It stops a wrong read of probe 46 if that run is slow, which protects the 28 Sep slot choice between the division rungs and Corwin/exp75. It also keeps exp75's runtime gate honest, so the probe slot is not wasted on partial coverage. It costs ~10 minutes of editing and uses no slots.
